title: Faithfulness Under the Distribution: A New Look at Attribution Evaluation
claim: Heuristic perturbations push evaluation samples out of distribution; guiding them back toward the data manifold with a learned score field keeps them in-distribution.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; schematic manifold plus 3D density and score-field plots
description: The left panel (a) is a schematic of the data space. A purple hatched rectangle labeled OOD Space contains a blue-outlined green grid blob labeled ID Space. A purple circle, marking other methods' masked samples, sits outside the blob. A green square, marking FUD's samples, sits inside it. Green arrows labeled Diffusion lead from the circle into the blob. To the left are noisy, corrupted chair photos labeled INS/DEL and INFID in purple. To the right is a clean chair photo labeled FUD (Ours) in green. The right panel (b) has two plots. (i) is a 3D density surface with three peaks and a viridis colorbar, overlaid with Langevin trajectories. (ii) is a 2D vector score field with a circle and three colored trajectories converging on modes. Purple marks OOD and green marks ID throughout.
caption: Overview of the FUD framework. (a) The left panel illustrates the core motivation of FUD: compared to conventional attribution evaluation metrics such as INS/DEL and INFID, which generate perturbed inputs drifting into the OOD space (purple area), FUD ensures that evaluation samples remain within the ID manifold (green area) by reconstructing masked regions via a score-based diffusion model. (b) The right panel shows how FUD leverages Langevin dynamics to guide inputs back toward the data manifold. Subfigure (i) visualizes Langevin trajectories in a toy 3D density; subfigure (ii) shows how the learned score field ∇x log pθ(x) steers samples from OOD to ID regions. The derivation of this score function is discussed in Section 3.3.
abstract: Evaluating the faithfulness of attribution methods remains an open challenge. Standard metrics such as Insertion and Deletion Scores rely on heuristic input perturbations (e.g., zeroing pixels), which often push samples out of the data distribution (OOD). This can distort model behavior and lead to unreliable evaluations. We propose FUD, a novel evaluation framework that reconstructs masked regions using score-based diffusion models to produce in-distribution, semantically coherent inputs. This distribution-aware approach avoids the common pitfalls of existing Attribution Evaluation Methods (AEMs) and yields assessments that more accurately reflect attribution faithfulness. Experiments across models show that FUD produces significantly different—and more reliable—judgments than prior approaches. Our implementation is available at: https://github.com/LMBTough/FUD.
